payload.stories:
Each slideshow realizes a named value prop from the pitch. Props, named once so the stories can cite them:
P1 reads that reach anywhere by name · P2 searches that see the working tree AND the record · P3 batched edits · P4 lints for the mechanical half · P5 four mandatory rounds of increasing scrutiny · P6 a reopen that actually reopens · P7 a shared judge that reaches the running lane · P8 a refusal instead of a confident wrong answer.
Evidence sides are deliberately EMPTY — they fill at validation, not here.

=====================================================================
S1 — THE GATE THAT REVIEWS ITSELF   [KILLER]   realizes P5, P6
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. An agent reaches a gate at the end of a milestone. It has built the thing, its tests are green, and it wants to move on. The owner is asleep.
Slide 2 · THE ASK. The evidence form shows the gate's own acceptance items — and four more fields it cannot leave blank: verify_round, validate_round, redteam_round, verdict. All four are required. It did not choose to run them; nothing asked it whether it would like to.
Slide 3 · THE TURN. In the validate round it reads the work against the REQUIREMENT REGISTER rather than against its own plan, and finds a requirement its own design violates — the design that claimed to satisfy it.
Slide 4 · THE VERDICT. It writes REOPEN, names the states, and the machine carries it out: those states and their whole downstream cone come back to life, the earlier fills marked superseded rather than erased.
Slide 5 · THE MORNING. The owner reads a gate that caught its own author. Not a green tick — a green tick with the case against it written underneath, and a record of what did not survive.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)
WHY KILLER: this is the iteration. If a gate can still pass without its rounds, nothing else here matters — and the proof standard is high, because this exact scenario failed once already: the rounds were required in writing, and every gate in the project's history passed without them.

=====================================================================
S2 — THE AGENT WHO STOPS WRITING SCRIPTS   [KILLER]   realizes P1, P2, P3
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. The agent needs to know how v1 solved a problem it is about to re-solve. The answer is in a file that is not in this worktree, in a revision that shipped weeks ago.
Slide 2 · THE OLD WAY. It writes a script. Not because it wants to — because the read lane cannot reach outside the iteration's root, and the search lane cannot see a git ref. The owner sees a script go by and asks why the tools it built are not being used.
Slide 3 · THE NEW WAY. One search, scoped to a ref. Matches come back WITH the lines around them, so the agent reads the answer instead of reading a line number and going back for a second call.
Slide 4 · THE EDIT. The fix touches ten places across five files. One batch call, atomic by construction: every edit is verified before any is written, so a bad match on the tenth means the first nine never happened.
Slide 5 · THE OUTCOME. No script. Nothing to declare, nothing to log, nothing to fix at the next retro.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)
WHY KILLER: the lane is judged by whether the honest path runs inside it. Six times in one day it did not, and each one cost an owner's evening.

=====================================================================
S3 — THE SECOND AGENT   [KILLER]   realizes P7
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. Two agents, two iterations, at the same time. One of them is improving the engine.
Slide 2 · THE TRAP. If each ran the engine from its own worktree, the two iterations would be judged by DIFFERENT machines — one collecting the review rounds, one not. A gate would stop meaning one thing.
Slide 3 · THE STEP. The engine change is promoted: trunk pulled current first, engine files only, the whole suite run IN TRUNK after the copy and before the commit, and on any failure trunk restored exactly as it was.
Slide 4 · THE TURN. The suite comes back red. Nothing is committed; the other agent never sees a broken judge. The refusal NAMES the failing test, so the fix takes a minute and not an hour.
Slide 5 · THE OUTCOME. Both agents run against one judge, and the one building the engine gets its own improvement in the same session.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)
WHY KILLER: the whole point is iterations that run alone and in parallel. Every alternative here — per-worktree engines, waiting for the close, asking the owner — breaks exactly when the second agent appears.

=====================================================================
S4 — THE WRONG ARGUMENT   realizes P8
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. The agent calls a tool and mistypes an argument name.
Slide 2 · THE OLD WAY. The value arrives as undefined, the tool coerces it into something plausible, and the answer comes back confident and wrong. The agent proceeds on it. Nothing anywhere is red.
Slide 3 · THE NEW WAY. Dispatch refuses: the clause, what was expected, what arrived, and the remedy with the argument names spelled out.
Slide 4 · THE FINE DISTINCTION. An argument that is ABSENT is not the same as one explicitly passed as null. The first is a mistake; the second is a deliberate statement. The guard learned this the hard way — its first version refused a legitimate null and became the very workaround pressure it was built to remove.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)

=====================================================================
S5 — THE CHECK THAT DOES NOT PRETEND   realizes P4
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. A gate asks whether the work adheres to the models, and whether every requirement has a verification method.
Slide 2 · THE HONEST ANSWER. It cannot be computed today — requirements are prose, not nodes, so nothing mechanical can join them to anything.
Slide 3 · THE TURN. The lint returns DEFER, with the reason stated, rather than PASS. A deferral is visible; a false pass is not.
Slide 4 · THE OUTCOME. The deferral carries a RAID entry naming what would have to change — items as nodes — and that is an owner's decision and its own iteration, not something to be quietly assumed here.
Slide 5 · THE RULE. Everything that CAN be checked mechanically is not left to the agent's judgement, because an agent judging its own work is the failure this whole iteration exists to fix.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)

=====================================================================
S6 — THE READER SIX MONTHS OUT   realizes P6
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. Someone opens this iteration's record long after it shipped, and finds a state that was filled twice.
Slide 2 · THE ASK. Which one is true, and why did the first one stop being true?
Slide 3 · THE ANSWER. The first fill is there, marked superseded. Between the two sits a reopened marker carrying the reason in the words of whoever ordered it.
Slide 4 · THE OUTCOME. The record shows a mind being changed, which is the only kind of record worth keeping. Nothing was deleted to make the current state look clean.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)

=====================================================================
S7 — THE OWNER READING CHAT   realizes P1, and the T3 tension
=====================================================================
Slide 1 · SETUP. The owner is away. Their entire view of the run is chat and the board.
Slide 2 · THE PROBLEM. The message says a requirement is satisfied and names it R3. The owner has never seen R3. The sentence reads as precision and carries nothing.
Slide 3 · THE TURN. Every id is expanded in the message that uses it, and where the plain phrase will do, the id does not appear at all.
Slide 4 · THE OUTCOME. The owner can adjudicate from what they were sent, which is the only thing they have.
EVIDENCE SIDE: (empty until validation)
